article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Hybrid
Genetics: Skunk × Haze
Breeder: Mr. Nice Seedbank
THC Content: 25%
CBD Content: N/A
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Sweet citrus, lemon, spicy herbs
Flowering Time (Indoor): 9–11 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: November
Indoor Yield: 350–500 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 500+ g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Intermediate to advanced

Skunk Haze comes from cannabis breeding at its most elemental: take two genetic families that helped define modern marijuana and allow their opposing qualities to meet in roughly equal measure. Mr. Nice Seedbank identifies the cultivar as 50% Skunk and 50% Haze, bred by Nevil Schoenmakers and Shantibaba . One half brings compactness, yield, pungency, and greater predictability; the other contributes height, cerebral intensity, longer flowering, incense-like complexity, and the restless energy associated with old Haze. The hybrid became a fixture of the 1990s-era breeding scene not because it was the quickest plant available, but because growers willing to accept several additional weeks of flowering could uncover exceptional combinations of resin, aroma, potency, and yield. Mr. Nice still describes it as one of the proven pillars of the cannabis world.

That history gives the strain a very different identity from contemporary hybrids engineered around dessert sweetness or extreme laboratory THC numbers. Properly grown flower can move from lemon and sweet fruit into spice, incense, herbs, earth, and unmistakable Skunk pungency. The experience tends to be similarly layered. Cerebral stimulation usually dominates early, encouraging conversation, sensory engagement, and wandering thought before a steadier physical calm begins to appear. Skunk Haze is consequently an old-school weed cultivar in the best sense: genetically influential, somewhat variable, less commercially convenient than a rapid indica, but capable of producing flowers with unusual depth.
Genetics and Lineage

Mr. Nice Seedbank lists the family breed simply and deliberately as 50% Skunk and 50% Haze. Although the cultivar is frequently summarized elsewhere as Skunk #1 × Haze, the breeder’s current official documentation does not provide a more specific parent-by-parent designation, so the most accurate reference is the breeder’s own formulation. Nevil and Shantibaba developed the line from genetics that had already become central to the emerging Dutch seed industry. Both families would ultimately appear throughout countless hybrids produced during the late twentieth century.

The Skunk side represents one of the fundamental building blocks of stabilized hybrid marijuana. Classic Skunk genetics combine Afghan and American tropical ancestry and were selected for vigor, relatively consistent flowering, substantial production, resin, and pungent aroma. Haze sits at almost the opposite horticultural extreme. Its tropical sativa ancestry is associated with tall plants, long flowering periods, narrower flowers, complex spice and incense aromas, and extremely cerebral effects. Combining the two allowed breeders to reduce some of Haze’s cultivation challenges without erasing its most desirable psychoactive and aromatic characteristics.

The importance of the pairing extends well beyond this strain page. Skunk/Haze breeding material became part of the foundation behind influential later hybrids, helping bridge long-flowering tropical cannabis with varieties growers could realistically maintain indoors. Mr. Nice continues to categorize Skunk Haze within its “Naturals – Old School Genetics” collection and specifically calls Skunk and Haze two of the most influential breeding lines of recent decades. That context matters more than attaching a fashionable contemporary family name to the cultivar: Skunk Haze sits close to the genetic foundation from which many later commercial weed strains were constructed.
Effects and Experience

The experience is primarily cerebral at the beginning. Mr. Nice explicitly characterizes Skunk Haze as capable of producing a distinctly cerebral effect, and that mental character is one of the clearest Haze contributions. The onset may heighten conversation, music, visual detail, curiosity, and associative thought rather than immediately slowing the body. In moderate amounts, experienced consumers may find it well suited to creative activity, social situations, long walks, music, or other environments where a mentally engaging high is desirable.

Skunk genetics keep the experience from behaving like an uncompromising tropical sativa. As the session develops, the initial mental movement often gains a more grounded physical component. The body can relax while the mind remains active, producing a middle ground between stimulating Haze and heavier Skunk-derived effects. Individual plants may lean noticeably toward one side of the family, however. A Haze-dominant phenotype can feel brighter and more expansive, while a Skunk-heavy plant may settle into a denser and calmer experience sooner.

Because Mr. Nice does not publish one modern THC percentage for the original cultivar, potency should be evaluated batch by batch. That is especially important with seed-grown old-school genetics, where chemical expression may vary more than in a single standardized commercial clone. Larger amounts of THC-rich cannabis can still produce racing thoughts, anxiety, short-term memory disruption, dry mouth, dizziness, and impaired coordination. A mentally energetic high does not mean reaction time or judgment remains unaffected.
Medical Benefits

The original Skunk Haze has a long association with medical cannabis culture , and Mr. Nice specifically notes that the cultivar has historically appealed to medical patients. That reputation should not, however, be interpreted as proof that the strain treats a specific condition. There are no controlled clinical trials demonstrating that Skunk Haze itself relieves pain, anxiety, depression, insomnia, or another disease.

Broader research into cannabis and cannabinoids provides a more responsible framework. Evidence suggests that certain cannabinoid preparations can produce modest improvements in some chronic pain conditions, while other research has examined nausea, appetite, sleep, and neurological symptoms. Results vary considerably according to the cannabinoids, dose, route of administration, and population studied. Named marijuana flower also varies chemically from crop to crop, making a strain name far less standardized than a medication used in a controlled trial.

People should also distinguish the original THC-oriented Skunk Haze from CBD Skunk Haze. Shantibaba later developed the separate CBD version through CBD Crew breeding, producing a cultivar averaging roughly 5–12% THC and 5–12% CBD with an intended ratio around 1:1. That is a different product with a very different cannabinoid profile. The original cultivar discussed here should not automatically be assigned those CBD levels simply because the names are similar.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

The aromatic character changes considerably depending on which side of the family dominates. Haze-heavy plants can bring citrus peel, lemon, dry spice, incense, herbs, and almost woody or church-like aromatic qualities. Skunk influence adds sweet pungency, earth, musk, and a heavier cannabis odor underneath. When the two sides meet evenly, the bouquet can be unusually complex: sweet fruit and lemon at the top, spicy herbs and incense through the middle, then earth and Skunk remaining after the brighter aromas fade.

Unlike many modern hybrids, sweetness does not necessarily translate into candy. Fruit character tends to feel more natural and botanical, with citrus accompanied by dry spice rather than syrup or pastry. Grinding the buds can release more of the pungent Skunk side, while combustion or vaporization may accentuate woody, herbal, and incense qualities inherited from Haze.

Mr. Nice does not publish an authoritative terpene laboratory panel for the original line, so assigning a permanent dominant-terpene ranking would create false precision. Old cultivars such as this are better understood through their documented sensory range and phenotype variation. Drying and curing become especially important for Haze-derived aromatics because the lighter citrus, floral, and incense qualities can disappear rapidly when marijuana is dried too warm or stored carelessly.
Growing Information

Skunk Haze is not difficult because it is fragile; it is demanding because its Haze heritage requires planning. Mr. Nice recommends the cultivar for experienced to advanced growers and lists both indoor and outdoor or greenhouse cultivation as suitable. Indoor flowering ranges from approximately 9–11 weeks, noticeably longer than compact commercial indicas but still manageable compared with extreme pure-Haze plants.

Expect significant phenotype variation in plant shape and flowering behavior. Haze-leaning individuals can stretch considerably after the light cycle changes, so indoor growers benefit from controlling plant height before flowering becomes established. Topping, tying, or screen-style canopy management where cultivation is legal can spread vigorous branches horizontally and help prevent the upper canopy from outrunning available vertical space. Skunk-dominant plants may remain somewhat stockier and finish toward the earlier end of the breeder’s window.

Indoor yield is officially listed at approximately 350–500 grams per square meter. Outdoors, Mr. Nice says production depends heavily on the length of the vegetative period but can exceed 500 grams per plant. Northern Hemisphere plants typically finish in November, though faster phenotypes may mature earlier; Southern Hemisphere cultivation is expected to conclude around May to June. Those dates make climate selection important. Late-finishing outdoor marijuana needs enough dry autumn weather to develop fully without persistent rain or excessive humidity around the flowers.

Resin production is a significant part of the breeder’s description. Mr. Nice specifically highlights the strain for hash makers, suggesting abundant trichome material in desirable selections. That resin potential makes environmental control increasingly important near maturity. Adequate airflow around flowers reduces stagnant humidity, while supporting taller branches can prevent bending as flowers add weight.

Post-harvest handling deserves patience. The entire attraction of a good Haze hybrid can be damaged by an overly rapid dry. A controlled drying period followed by curing allows the lemon, fruit, spice, incense, and Skunk layers to separate more clearly. Old-school Haze-derived weed can also change noticeably during curing, with sharper green or herbal notes gradually becoming smoother and more integrated.
FAQ
What strain is Skunk Haze?

Skunk Haze is a classic 50% Skunk / 50% Haze hybrid bred by Nevil Schoenmakers and Shantibaba and maintained by Mr. Nice Seedbank. It combines two foundational cannabis families to produce a cerebral, resinous, productive old-school hybrid.
Is Skunk Haze the same as CBD Skunk Haze?

No. The original Skunk Haze is the classic Nevil and Shantibaba line. CBD Skunk Haze is a later CBD-enriched cultivar developed through CBD Crew breeding and averages roughly 5–12% THC and 5–12% CBD. The two should be treated as separate strains.
Is Skunk Haze indica or sativa?

Mr. Nice classifies the family breed as exactly 50% Skunk and 50% Haze. Individual plants can lean toward either side, with Haze-dominant phenotypes generally stretching more and expressing stronger cerebral qualities.
How long does Skunk Haze take to flower?
Mr. Nice lists approximately 9–11 weeks indoors. Outdoors, Northern Hemisphere plants normally finish around November, although some phenotypes can mature earlier.
How much does Skunk Haze yield?
The breeder lists approximately 350–500 g/m² indoors. Outdoors, plants can exceed 500 grams each when given sufficient vegetative time and favorable growing conditions.
Final Thoughts on Skunk Haze

Skunk Haze is important because there is almost nothing unnecessary in its genetic concept. Skunk provides production, vigor, pungency, and a more manageable growing pattern. Haze brings cerebral intensity, longer aromatic development, spice, incense, citrus, and the vertical energy of tropical cannabis. Rather than hiding either parent beneath layers of newer genetics, Nevil and Shantibaba built the cultivar around an even 50/50 meeting of two foundational families.

Its cultivation requirements reflect that heritage. Nine to eleven weeks of flowering is slower than modern commercial indica hybrids, and November outdoor maturity limits the climates where the plant can finish comfortably. In return, growers can see indoor production around 350–500 g/m², outdoor plants exceeding 500 grams, abundant resin, meaningful phenotype diversity, and flower that preserves the unmistakable character of classic Skunk/Haze marijuana. Mr. Nice’s recommendation to experienced growers is therefore appropriate: the strain rewards someone prepared to manage stretch and allow the plant enough time to finish properly.

For consumers, the defining quality is the way the experience remains mentally engaging without behaving like an untouched equatorial sativa. Citrus, spice, incense, earth, sweet fruit, herbs, and Skunk create an aromatic profile far removed from contemporary dessert weed, while the effect can move from cerebral stimulation toward a steadier hybrid balance.

Most importantly, Skunk Haze should not be confused with CBD Skunk Haze. The latter is a separate medicinally oriented CBD Crew development with substantially different cannabinoid targets. The original version is the old-school Nevil and Shantibaba cultivar: half Skunk, half Haze, longer flowering than commercial indicas, highly resinous, productive, and representative of two genetic families that helped shape much of the cannabis breeding that followed.
